storyTitle: Tower Hamlets Council to acquire Marsh Wall properties for 180 new temporary homes
headline: Tower Hamlets approves 180 homes at Marsh Wall

watchability.targetAudience: Tower Hamlets residents and local taxpayers
watchability.hook: Tower Hamlets approves 180 homes at Marsh Wall
watchability.hookStyle: Immediate factual council decision and resident impact
watchability.localRelevance: Directly affects Tower Hamlets residents and council services

claims.statement: Tower Hamlets Council approved leasing four office buildings on Marsh Wall for conversion into temporary housing.
claims.sourceQuote: Tower Hamlets Council's Cabinet has approved plans to acquire four commercial office buildings in Marsh Wall for conversion into approximately 180 new homes for temporary accommodation.

claims.statement: The converted properties will provide 167 two-bedroom and 13 three-bedroom self-contained family units.
claims.sourceQuote: The conversion of these buildings is anticipated to provide 167 two-bedroom and 13 three-bedroom self-contained family units.

claims.statement: The scheme will be funded through General Fund borrowing while facing construction and lease risks.
claims.sourceQuote: The scheme is proposed to be funded through General Fund borrowing, and further detailed design, planning, and financial assessments will be required before the lease is finalised.

takeawayCard.title: Ending Out-of-Borough Moves
takeawayCard.subtitle: Homeless families remain near local schools and jobs.

keyPoints: Four office buildings will be converted into approximately 180 temporary family homes.
The scheme creates 167 two-bedroom and 13 three-bedroom self-contained family units locally.
General Fund borrowing will finance the acquisition despite identified construction cost risks.
